subject: Post-signature MAP: staggered rollout, canary windows, and surge rollback plan
messages:

Subject: Signed agreement + request for a detailed MAP

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Great to get the contract over the line — signatures are attached on our side. Thanks for the responsiveness. Before we schedule the kickoff, our engineering and security teams asked for a single-sheet mutual action plan (MAP) that outlines:

- High-level rollout milestones (canary window, broader ramp)
- Migration approach for our legacy inference calls (approx. 20% of traffic)
- Minimum training schedule for support & ops (~2 sessions?)
- Contingency/rollback triggers and an ops escalation path

Can you send a draft MAP and a short canary checklist we can share with our SREs? We have a preferred go-live window between Aug 15–31 but are open to a staged approach. Also please include any compliance artifacts we can pre-share with our auditors (SOC 2 evidence pointer).

Thanks,
Rachel

HealthBridge Labs

Hi Rachel — congrats and welcome aboard!

Attached is an initial MAP workbook (HB4721_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short canary-ops checklist PDF. Summary of the plan (top-level):

1) Staged rollout (recommended):
   - Phase 0: Pre-go-live (config + test harness) — Target: Aug 1–7
   - Phase 1: Canary (5% traffic routing to Redwood inference, 48–72h watch) — Target: Aug 15–18
   - Phase 2: Gradual ramp (5% -> 50% over 2 weeks) — Aug 19–31
   - Phase 3: Full cutover (post acceptance; fallback available for 7 days) — early Sep

2) Migration approach:
   - Side-by-side routing for legacy endpoints; we’ll run shadow inference for a week before canary to validate outputs and latencies.
   - A simple header-based router (x-hb-route: canary) for 5% sampling so you can control membership server-side.

3) Training & enablement:
   - Two live sessions (90 min) for SREs + App owners covering: observability, fallback, and manual rollback.
   - One ops tabletop drill (60 min) scheduled during canary window to rehearse rollback.

4) Rollback & surge handling:
   - Automated fallback if error-rate > 2% or median P95 latency degrades > 200ms for 30m.
   - Manual escalation path: on-call SRE (HealthBridge) -> Redwood duty (Ben) -> Redwood Eng manager (Marissa).

I've left placeholders in the MAP workbook for dates and names so we can finalize during kickoff. Canary checklist items in the PDF include telemetry knobs, required logs, and test prompts to validate model quality.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the preferred canary start date (Aug 15 looks OK per your note)?
- Who from HB SRE should join the tabletop drill (name + pager)?
- Any blockers from procurement for sharing SOC 2 links internally?

Best,
Sofia Ivánova
Principal Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HB4721_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), canary-ops-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Sofia — leaving a few operational notes inline: 

- Canary sizing: 5% is good for functional validation, but for latency and cache-warmth we recommend a 24–36 hour burst to 10% during the second canary day. That helps surface KV cache cold-starts.
- Shadow period: we should run shadow inference on production traffic for 72 hours before the canary to capture realistic distributions; we can keep results internal to HB if you prefer.
- Data retention for logs and traces: default retention is 90d; if HB needs longer for audits, we can extend to 365d as an add-on — budget note for procurement.

I've attached a short ops checklist (canary-ops-checklist.pdf) with exact alert thresholds and the rollback runbook. Ben — can you confirm Redwood on-call for the proposed windows? Vanessa — I'll need you to coordinate the training calendar (two sessions + tabletop).

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary-ops-checklist.pdf (pdf)

- SRE attendees for the tabletop: Aaron Patel (pager: aaron.p@healthbridge.com) and Priya Menon (priya.m@healthbridge.com).

If you can confirm those items and drop the final MAP workbook with filled dates we’ll lock the kickoff.

—Rachel
